A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Artificial Hippocampus Networks research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original AHN benchmark results, training ablations, a PG19 case study, gradient visualization, and appendix evaluations on RULER.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds inference-window experiments and a pure-RNN ablation.

M1.justification: The recurrent compression procedure, three AHN variants, attention integration, and frozen-backbone KL self-distillation remain unchanged. V2 clarifies shared QKV projections and gate parameterization without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use ChatQA2, LV-Eval, InfiniteBench, LongBench, PG19, and RULER. V2 identifies AceMath as the source of the existing gradient example; the example itself is unchanged. Its short-context and pretraining discussions introduce no additional empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds a pure-RNN comparator against Sinks+SWA and the combined AHN framework in Table 8. Existing benchmark comparator sets are retained. Infini-attention, MiL, LoLCATs, and HQLT receive expanded discussion, but are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 1k–96k inference-window sweep with 128 attention sinks on the existing 128k benchmarks. Table 7 introduces a separate training-FLOP calculation using full-parameter next-token training, batch size 128, 24k sequences, and an 8k window. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; newly disclosed training details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends design analysis through the LV-Eval/InfiniteBench window-size sweep, the attention-removal ablation in Appendix E, and training-efficiency calculations in Appendix D. The earlier LongBench sensitivity study is retained as Figure 7, while the original training ablations, gradient example, and RULER failure analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. V2's detailed training-window sampling rules describe training randomization, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds window-sensitivity curves, training-FLOP estimates, absolute inference costs, and pure-RNN scores of 0.04/1.19 versus 6.54/16.93 for the combined framework on LV-Eval/InfiniteBench. Existing benchmark accuracy tables remain unchanged. Some Table 2 efficiency values change, including the 7B AHN model-FLOP ratio from 65.4% to 65.6%.

T1.justification: The recurrence equations, attention formulation, KL objective, gradient definition, and Table 1 complexity expressions are retained. Equation renumbering and explicit gate-weight parameterization elaborate existing mathematics without adding a substantive theoretical result, assumption, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same two contributions and the claim of competitive long-context performance with lower computation and cache requirements. V2 foregrounds the existing self-distillation scheme and 32k inference configuration without changing the central scientific claims.

C2.justification: V2 proposes attention dilution as an explanation for large-window degradation and interprets the pure-RNN ablation as evidence that attention remains necessary. It retains the exact-recall limitation but removes v1's explicit base-model-capacity caveat and associated full-parameter-training future direction.

D1.justification: V2 supplies previously missing sink/window sampling candidates and filters, the 24k training limit, 1B-token budget, 740 updates, and approximately 10 hours on 32 A100 GPUs for the 7B model. It also specifies trainable gate weights and the gradient example's source, sequence length, and window. These substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds nine cited works and substantially expands positioning against hybrid attention–RNN methods. Section 4 and Appendix F compare AHN with Infini-attention, MiL, LoLCATs, and HQLT across architecture, window size, target tasks, and training requirements.

P1.justification: Related work moves after the experiments, and the abstract, implementation explanations, ablation discussion, and appendix organization expand. Much of the original prose and section content remains intact, so this is a bounded restructuring rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds a two-panel window-sensitivity figure and Tables 7–9 for training costs, component ablation, and detailed inference costs. The original LongBench Figure 4 becomes an enlarged appendix Figure 7. Diagram styling, captions, and the abstract layout are also revised, substantially expanding and reorganizing the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The explicit training recipe improves reproducibility, while the new window-size study and pure-RNN control strengthen support for existing design choices. Expanded related-work comparisons clarify positioning. Core benchmark conclusions remain unchanged, and removing the base-capacity caveat slightly weakens qualification; overall, the evidence supports a useful but limited improvement.
